description: Marketing campaigns across channels. Budget vs spend tracks overrun. Links to leads via leads.campaign_id.
Compensation change history. One row per comp event (new hire, merit, promotion, adjustment). Partitioned by effective_date, clustered by employee_id. Highly sensitive — restricted access.
Addresses for customer accounts. Multiple addresses per customer (billing, shipping, HQ).
People at customer accounts. Multiple contacts per customer. is_primary identifies the main point of contact; is_decision_maker flags economic buyers.
B2B customer accounts. One row per company (logo). Clustered by segment, status. Source of truth for account ownership and LTV.
Organizational departments. Self-referencing via parent_department_id to form the department tree. Cost centers map to finance GL codes.
SCD-style time-series of employee role changes. One row per role held. end_date IS NULL for the current role. Used for tenure, promotion velocity, and reorg analysis.
Junction table tracking employee enrollments in training courses.
All ACME employees, past and present. Contains current role snapshot; see employee_role_history for time-series role changes. Clustered by department_id, employment_status.
Invoices issued to customers. Partitioned by issue_date, clustered by status. Linked to subscription or order (or both).
Canonical job titles with level and salary band. Employees reference this table to avoid free-text title drift.
Top-of-funnel leads prior to qualification. Partitioned by DATE(created_at), clustered by status. Converts to customers via converted_customer_id.
Physical ACME offices worldwide. One row per office location. Source of truth for employee work locations and regional capacity planning.
Sales opportunities (deals). Partitioned by close_date, clustered by stage. Core pipeline and forecast table.
Line items on orders. Multiple rows per order.
One-time orders (non-subscription). Partitioned by order_date, clustered by status. Includes services and perpetual licenses.
Payment transactions against invoices. Partitioned by DATE(paid_at), clustered by status. May include refunds (status = refunded).
Half-yearly performance reviews. One row per employee per review period.
Product category tree. Self-referencing via parent_category_id.
Sellable products and services. Includes software (on-prem + SaaS), services, and training. Cost is internal unit cost for margin analysis.
Employee allocations to projects. Multiple rows per employee / project possible over time.
Internal projects (cross-functional initiatives). Budget/spend tracks overrun. project_lead_id is the accountable DRI.
Price quotes generated against opportunities. Version increments on each revision; the highest-version accepted row represents the final deal.
Logged sales activities: calls, emails, meetings, demos. Partitioned by DATE(activity_at). Can link to opportunity, lead, or contact.
SaaS subscriptions (recurring revenue). Partitioned by start_date, clustered by status. Source of truth for MRR/ARR.
Customer support tickets. Partitioned by DATE(created_at), clustered by status, priority. SLA timestamps: first_response_at, resolved_at.
Teams within departments. A department typically has multiple teams. Used for squad-level reporting and Slack routing.
Chronological comments on support tickets. Partitioned by DATE(created_at). Includes internal-only notes (is_internal=TRUE).
Employee time-off requests. Partitioned by start_date.
Catalog of training courses available to employees, internal or external.
Contracts with vendors. Tracks annual spend and auto-renewal for procurement / FP&A.
Third-party vendors / suppliers. Risk rating drives security review cadence.
Web analytics events from acme.example. Partitioned by DATE(event_at), clustered by event_type, utm_source. High-volume; prefer partition-pruned queries.
